answer.evidence: Rows 0-37 are a large roof surface seen from above. It has a parapet border, a caved-in dark hole with slabs and rebar, and a light front-edge line at row 37 with darker shadow below. Below it the front face runs rows 38-63 (26 rows): a fascia panel at rows 38-46 and a shutter with a torn corner at rows 47-63. The roof is drawn quite flat and top-down, but the edge line and the 26-row front face give a roof plus front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate's visible tones per tile (12) match house-h101_0 (12) and beat house-h112_0-stone (10). Near-flat coverage is 7% against 0% in both references, so it has some flat fill. The grey concrete roof and the fascia panel are large, mostly even areas with only sparse speckle and rust dots. The roof ramp shows about 4 steps (highlight rim, mid, dark, hole), while the references use 5-6 steps per material with per-tile scallops, plaster speckle and stones shaded one by one. 28% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, against 7-9% in the references, so the outline is partly near-black around the hole and the shutter. It is not a uniform sticker line, since the parapet edge is tinted grey. The shutter and the broken slab have some detail, but the shutter is a flat dark block with a few rust flecks. Overall the piece is competent but shallower and flatter than the references, so with the flat fills and the partly neutral outline I fail it on a when-in-doubt basis.
